newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 agrees strong dollar good for all - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: G10 agrees strong dollar good for all - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the Group of 10 (G10) central banks governors' committee agreed a strong dollar was in everyone's interest.

Tietmeyer, speaking as chairman of the G10 central bank governors' committee, also said the stance of monetary policy in continental Europe was appropriate and could not do more to encourage growth for the time being.
He said Europe's problems could not be solved by monetary policy. It was important that structural reforms of fiscal situations, social security and labour markets continue.
The G10 central bankers, at their monthly meeting, discussed the exchange rate situation.
"We all agreed further dollar development is important and a strong dollar is in the interest of all," Tietmeyer told reporters after the meeting.
"This is the common position of the G10," he added.
The G10 comprises the central banks of the U.S., Canada, Japan, Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, Italy and England.
Tietmeyer said monetary policy could not do more for Europe's economy at present.
"The monetary policy is in an appropriate stance and can't do more for the time being," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyer stressed that it was important that structural reforms be continued and addressed even stronger if a cyclical upturn was underway.

"Especially in continental European countries, it is important that the structural reforms are now continued and addressed even stronger if the cyclical upturn will continue because fiscal policies and the adjustment process in social security systems are an absolute priority," Tietmeyer said.
"Besides that an increase in labour flexibility is a necessity for lasting growth and for job creation," Tietmeyer said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
